After his initial arrest following the SWAT standoff on February 10th, Richard Colbert posted
Bond and was released from the Broward County Jail a few days later.
However, his freedom only lasted a matter of days.
On February 17th, Richard violated the conditions of his pre-trial release after he was caught
using a cell phone and posting on social media something explicitly prohibited under the terms
of his bond.
That same day, police were also called to a plantation neighborhood after reports that
Richard had blocked a public roadway using traffic cones and foliage, creating a disturbance
in the area.
When officers attempted to detain him, Richard fled on foot, jumping multiple fences
and allegedly entering several private homes and screened-in patios in an attempt to hide from police.
Following his second bond hearing on February 21st, 2006, his bail was set at $47,000.
As of May 2006, Richard Colbert is facing a total of six active charges in Broward County, Florida,
stemming from the combined February incidents.
The felony charges include, written or electronic threats to kill,
burglary of an occupied dwelling unarmed, times three, misdemeanor, resisting, obstruction,
obstructing an officer without violence and obstructing a highway or public road.
Richard was also hit with additional pretrial infractions after violating the conditions of his
original $20,000 bond after the SWAT intervention incident.
While there is no confirmation on whether he remains in jail, legal reports from late February
stated that Richard pleaded not guilty to all charges and formally requested a jury trial.
